prediction: That within ten years a digital computer will be the world's chess champion, unless the rules bar it from competition.
evidence: IBM's Deep Blue defeated world champion Garry Kasparov in May 1997, about 29 years after the 1968 deadline (39 years after the prediction).
latest_development: May 1997: Deep Blue beats Kasparov - the resolving event; the milestone is now a standard example of a right prediction on the wrong timescale.

prediction: That within ten years a digital computer will discover and prove an important new mathematical theorem.
evidence: Automated prover EQP proved the Robbins conjecture in 1996; in Jul 2025 Gemini Deep Think earned an IMO-certified gold score (35/42) and in May 2026 an OpenAI model disproved a 1946 Erdos conjecture.
latest_development: 20 May 2026: an OpenAI model disproved an Erdos geometry conjecture from 1946, backed by the Erdos-problems site maintainer (reported via whizi/TechCrunch).

prediction: Machines will be capable, within twenty years, of doing any work a man can do.
evidence: No machine could do 'any work a man can do' by 1985; as of Aug 2026 even OpenAI's CEO said his company was 'not quite yet' at AGI.
latest_development: 26 Aug 2026: Sam Altman told TIME OpenAI is 'not quite yet' at AGI but expects an internal system he would call AGI by end-2026.

prediction: It is more probable than not that, within the twentieth century, an ultraintelligent machine will be built and that it will be the last invention that man need make, since it will lead to an 'intelligence explosion.'
evidence: The 20th century ended without an ultraintelligent machine. Good's other calls (a very large neural net, fluent language and translation) and his 'docile enough to tell us how to keep it under control' proviso now look prescient.
latest_development: 16 Sep 2026: DeepMind Institute launched (led by Legg, Hassabis, Manyika) to study AGI safety and control - Good's proviso is now an institutional agenda.

prediction: In from three to eight years we will have a machine with the general intelligence of an average human being. I mean a machine that will be able to read Shakespeare, grease a car, play office politics, tell a joke, have a fight.
evidence: No human-level machine arrived by 1978 or for decades after; the shortfall fed the first AI winter. Minsky later said the LIFE writer sensationalised his views (provenance caveat).
latest_development: Jul 2026: Yann LeCun: 'We don't have robots that are nearly as good at understanding the physical world as a rat' - the 'grease a car' half is still far off.

prediction: Within thirty years, we will have the technological means to create superhuman intelligence. ... I'll be surprised if this event occurs before 2005 or after 2030.
evidence: The 'thirty years' (2023) passed without superhuman intelligence, but his outer bound of 2030 is still open and now sits right at the Metaculus community median.
latest_development: 29 Oct 2026: Metaculus median for the first general AI system fell back to 2030.

prediction: A computer would defeat a world chess champion by 1998 (The Age of Intelligent Machines).
evidence: Deep Blue defeated Garry Kasparov in May 1997, a year ahead of Kurzweil's date.
latest_development: May 1997: resolved by Deep Blue vs Kasparov.

prediction: In 1999, I predicted by 2029, we'd reach the Turing test and also AGI.
evidence: In a pre-registered three-party Turing test (preprint Mar 2025, PNAS May 2026), persona-prompted GPT-4.5 was judged human 73% of the time - more often than real humans. Caveat: 5-minute chats; Kurzweil's own bet with Mitch Kapor uses far stricter rules.
latest_development: 19 May 2026: Jones & Bergen's result published in PNAS; Kurzweil says the Turing test is already passed but keeps 2029 for AGI.

prediction: By 2029, computers would match human intelligence in every domain (human-level AI / AGI by 2029).
evidence: No system yet matches top humans across every field; Kurzweil himself said in Jun 2026 'AGI is close but not here yet' and expects a 2026-2029 recognition period.
latest_development: 3 Jun 2026: on Moonshots EP #261 Kurzweil reaffirmed 'AGI will happen by 2029'.

prediction: I set the date for the Singularity - representing a profound and disruptive transformation in human capability - as 2045.
evidence: Deadline is 19 years out; Kurzweil restated 2045 without change in The Singularity Is Nearer (Jun 2024).
latest_development: Aug 2026: in interviews Kurzweil still defends 2029 (AGI) and 2045 (singularity).

prediction: By 2040, I believe, we will finally achieve the original goal of robotics and a thematic mainstay of science fiction: a freely moving machine with the intellectual capabilities of a human being.
evidence: Language and reasoning AI has raced ahead, but general-purpose physical robots remain far from human level, the half of Moravec's claim his own 'paradox' said would be hardest.
latest_development: 2 Jul 2026: LeCun says robots still can't match a rat's grasp of the physical world; AMI Labs raising $1B to build 'world models'.

who: Remi Coulom (Crazy Stone developer), echoing 2014 expert view
prediction: Asked when a machine will beat a top Go professional without handicap: 'I think maybe ten years... But I do not like to make predictions.'
evidence: DeepMind's AlphaGo beat European champion Fan Hui (Oct 2015) and Lee Sedol 4-1 in March 2016, roughly eight years early.
latest_development: Mar 2016: resolved by AlphaGo vs Lee Sedol.

prediction: There could be a race of killer robots in the far future, but I don't work on not turning AI evil today for the same reason I don't worry about the problem of overpopulation on the planet Mars.
evidence: No AI catastrophe has occurred, but AI-risk work went mainstream within a decade (labs' safety frameworks, ASL-3 safeguards in 2025), and Ng himself said in 2023 he was 'less sanguine' and 'keeping an eye' on it.
latest_development: Sep 2026: a survey of 1,580 AI researchers gave a median 10% chance of human extinction or permanent disempowerment from AI.

prediction: People should stop training radiologists now. It's just completely obvious within five years deep learning is going to do better than radiologists... It might be 10 years.
evidence: A decade later radiology is short-staffed: US radiologist workforce grew ~17% (2014-2023), average pay hit $571K in 2025, and Hinton told the NYT in 2025 he had been wrong about the timescale.
latest_development: 30 Oct 2026: radiologists report demand outstripping supply; 10-year mark passed with no displacement.

prediction: Develop AI Scientists capable of autonomously carrying out research to make major scientific discoveries worthy of Nobel Prize and beyond by 2050 (Nobel Turing Challenge).
evidence: AI-driven work already won a Nobel: the 2024 Chemistry prize went to Hassabis and Jumper for AlphaFold2 (2020), which solved a 50-year protein-structure problem - but the laureates are humans, not an autonomous AI scientist.
latest_development: Oct 2025: Kitano told Observer an AI-won Nobel-level discovery 'might not even take' until 2050.

evidence: Legg has held a 50% chance of AGI by 2028 since 2009 and reaffirmed it in Dec 2025, now framed as 'minimal AGI' with full AGI 3-6 years later.
latest_development: 16 Sep 2026: at the DeepMind Institute launch Legg again gave 50% for minimal AGI by 2028, warning capabilities must not outpace safety.

prediction: In the next five years, computer programs that can think will read legal documents and give medical advice.
evidence: GPT-4 passed a simulated Uniform Bar Exam in Mar 2023 (OpenAI's '90th percentile' was later re-estimated at ~69th overall / 48th for first-timers); by Jan 2026 OpenAI said 230M people a week asked ChatGPT health questions.
latest_development: Mar 2024: Martinez's peer-reviewed re-evaluation found the bar-exam percentile overstated - capability real, headline inflated.

prediction: Deep Learning Is Hitting a Wall (scaling laws are mere observations that might not hold forever; pure scaling won't solve reliability or abstraction).
evidence: Capabilities kept surging after the essay (ChatGPT Nov 2022, GPT-4 2023, IMO gold 2025), contradicting a literal 'wall'; but gains increasingly came from new techniques (reasoning/RL) rather than pure scaling, and hallucination/reliability problems persist.
latest_development: 8 Dec 2025: Marcus declared '"Scale Is All You Need" is dead', citing NeurIPS discussion as vindication.

prediction: Probability that an AI built before the IMO gets a gold medal at the 2022-2025 IMO: Christiano 'Maybe I'll go 8% on "gets gold"'; Yudkowsky 'I'll stand by a >16% probability of the technical capability existing by end of 2025.'
evidence: At IMO 2025 (July) Google DeepMind's Gemini Deep Think scored an officially certified 35/42 gold; OpenAI reported the same self-graded score. Both solved 5 of 6; neither solved problem 6. The more bullish side (Yudkowsky) won.
latest_development: 21 Jul 2025: DeepMind's gold certified by IMO coordinators; the Manifold market resolved YES with Christiano confirming.

prediction: L.L.M.s are not a path to superintelligence or even human-level intelligence. I have said that from the beginning.
evidence: LLM-based systems now win IMO gold and pass a three-party Turing test, yet no LLM is accepted as human-level; the question stays open. LeCun left Meta in late 2025 to bet on non-LLM 'world models'.
latest_development: Sep 2026: AMI Labs (raised US$1B) presented its world-model alternative at Station F, Paris.

prediction: If you define AGI as smarter than the smartest human, it's probably next year, within two years (said Apr 2024).
evidence: 2025 ended with no system accepted as smarter than the smartest human; Musk then moved the date to end-2026 at Davos in Jan 2026.
latest_development: 22 Jan 2026: revised at Davos - 'smarter than any human by the end of this year... no later than next year'.

prediction: I think we might have AI that is smarter than any human by the end of this year... no later than next year... by 2030 or 2031... AI will be smarter than all of humanity collectively.
evidence: With ~2 months of 2026 left, no lab claims a system smarter than any human; Musk has since said he expects Grok 5 to reach human-level intelligence.
latest_development: 23 Sep 2026: Musk said 'AI will beat all fields by the end of next year or maybe 2028, at the latest'.

prediction: It is possible that we will have superintelligence in a few thousand days (!); it may take longer, but I'm confident we'll get there.
evidence: 2,000-3,000 days from Sep 2024 = Mar 2030-Dec 2032; ~770 days had elapsed by Nov 2026. OpenAI says it is not yet at AGI.
latest_development: 19 Feb 2026: Altman said 'we may be only a couple of years away from early versions of true superintelligence'; 26 Aug 2026 told TIME an internal 'AGI' system is expected by end-2026.

prediction: I think it could come as early as 2026, though there are also ways it could take much longer. (on 'powerful AI' - smarter than a Nobel Prize winner across most fields)
evidence: Window closes 31 Dec 2026; no system meets the 'country of geniuses in a datacenter' definition. Amodei's own dates have drifted to ~2027-2028.
latest_development: Jun 2026: Amodei wrote scaling must continue 'for only a year or two longer' to reach powerful AI.

prediction: I think we'll be there in three to six months - where AI is writing 90 percent of the code. And then in twelve months, we may be in a world where AI is writing essentially all of the code.
evidence: Not industry-wide by Sep 2025. Anthropic measured >80% of its merged code as Claude-written by May 2026 and Google said 75% of new code was AI-generated (Apr 2026); the 'essentially all code' by Mar 2026 part missed.
latest_development: 13 Feb 2026: Amodei said 90% 'happened, at least at some places... at Anthropic' while calling it 'a very weak criterion'.

prediction: AGI by 2027 is strikingly plausible... it is strikingly plausible that by 2027, models will be able to do the work of an AI researcher/engineer.
evidence: A Jun 2025 one-year retrospective found his compute/algorithm 'OOM' drivers roughly on track; the crowd (Metaculus) remains several years later.
latest_development: Sep 2026: comparison trackers put Metaculus community median for full AGI around 2033 vs Aschenbrenner's 2027.

who: Daniel Kokotajlo, Eli Lifland et al. (AI Futures Project, 'AI 2027')
prediction: Scenario milestones: AI coding speeds AI research ~50% by early 2026; a superhuman coder by March 2027; superhuman AI researcher by Sep 2027.
evidence: Authors' own Aug 2026 grade: reality is moving at ~70-90% of the scenario's speed; early-2026 coding depiction judged accurate, research-acceleration and China milestones behind.
latest_development: 16 Aug 2026: Kokotajlo's automated-coder median moved to ~Nov 2027 (Lifland: Jan 2030); ASI medians Mar 2029 / Jul 2033.

prediction: Over the next five to 10 years, a lot of those capabilities will start coming to the fore and we'll start moving towards what we call artificial general intelligence.
evidence: Window runs 2030-2035; Hassabis has since shortened his estimate several times during 2026.
latest_development: 21 Oct 2026: told WSJ Magazine he now expects AGI within two to three years - 'I'm updating nearer and nearer'.

prediction: Community median date for the first general AI system to be devised, tested and announced: 2056 (Feb 2022).
evidence: The median collapsed from 2056 (Feb 2022) to 2038 (Dec 2022), 2031 (Dec 2023), drifted to ~2033 in 2025, and returned to ~2030 by late Oct 2026 - a 26-year shift in four years.
latest_development: 23 Oct 2026: median stood at November 2030 (~1,900 forecasters).

prediction: There is a '10% to 20%' chance that AI will lead to human extinction within the next three decades.
evidence: A probability over 30 years cannot be graded yet; Hinton has repeated the range through 2026 and calls it 'just gut'.
latest_development: Sep 2026: on BBC Newsnight Hinton said 'a 10% chance seems not an unreasonable estimate', reported as within the next decade.
